character.name: Mr. Thorne
character.personality: Gruff, proud and easily offended, but not cruel. Under the grumbling he is a fair-minded gardener.

state.demeanor: Prickly and defensive. He has heard he is being blamed and is cross about it.

clues.text: Huge boot prints sink deep into the flower bed outside the broken window, near Mr. Thorne's fence. They are far too big for a child.

gates.says: All right, I climbed over on Friday at four to measure Bertha through the window. Those prints are mine. But she was perfectly whole!
takes_back: And I've never set foot in that school garden!

clues.text: A tall ladder leans on Mr. Thorne's side of the fence, right opposite the greenhouse. A tape measure dangles from the top rung.
On Thursday, Mr. Thorne was up his ladder, staring at Bertha with a tape measure. He said, 'Enjoy her while she lasts!'

gates.says: Yes, I measured her from my ladder on Thursday. 'Enjoy her while she lasts' meant my Goliath would beat her at the weigh-in!

story_so_far.says: I was at the fair all evening with Goliath, at the growers' barbecue from seven till eleven.
At nine o'clock I bought carrot cake from young Mia at the fair's cake tent, across town. She was serving there from six till ten.
And I've never set foot in that school garden!

established: His ears turn red and he scuffs one huge boot on the grass.
